entries.sanskrit:
त्रिंशे तु कायकान्तादि- लालनाकुल-चेतसाम् ।

कामिनां तामसी पापाद् अधोगतिर् उदीर्यते ॥

काल-प्रभाव-वर्णन-पूर्वकं वैराग्याय विचित्र-कर्म-कृतां संसृतिम् अध्याय-त्रयेण प्रपञ्चयति । तस्यैतस्य बलिनः कालस्य । बलिनेति वा पाठः । काल्यमानो विचाल्यमानोऽपि । वायोर् विक्रमं यथा मेघ-पङ्क्तिर् न वेद ॥१॥
word_for_word: of those whose minds are absorbed in pampering the body, spouse, and the like
of sensualists; those driven by desire
with a description of Time’s power preceding it
of those who perform varied actions
or the reading is balinā, “by mighty [Time]”
a bank; a row of clouds
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
triṃśe tu kāyakāntādi- lālanākula-cetasām |

kāmināṃ tāmasī pāpād adhogatir udīryate ||

kāla-prabhāva-varṇana-pūrvakaṃ vairāgyāya vicitra-karma-kṛtāṃ saṃsṛtim adhyāya-trayeṇa prapañcayati | tasyaitasya balinaḥ kālasya | balineti vā pāṭhaḥ | kālyamāno vicālyamāno’pi | vāyor vikramaṃ yathā megha-paṅktir na veda ||1||
entries.literal_english: In the thirtieth chapter, the dark downward destination caused by sin is described for sensualists absorbed in pampering the body, spouse, and the like. The commentator says that, with Time’s power described first, he elaborates over three chapters the transmigration of those who perform varied actions, for the sake of detachment. “Of this mighty Time” has the alternative reading “by mighty [Time].” Though harried by Time and shaken, a person does not perceive its force, just as a bank of clouds does not perceive the force of the wind.

entries.sanskrit: दुराशयत्वम् आह---आक्षिप्त आत्मा इन्द्रियाणि च यस्य । कया ? असतीनां पुंश्चलीनाम् अपि रहसि रचितया सम्भोगादि-रूपया । मधुर-भाषिणां शिशूनाम् आलापैश् च । सुखवन् मन्यत इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥८॥ कूटाः वित्त-शाठ्यादि-बहुला धर्मा येषु दुःख-प्रधानेषु ॥९॥
word_for_word: in the form of sexual enjoyment and the like
thus it connects grammatically with what follows
abounding in financial deceit and the like
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: durāśayatvam āha---ākṣipta ātmā indriyāṇi ca yasya | kayā ? asatīnāṃ puṃścalīnām api rahasi racitayā sambhogādi-rūpayā | madhura-bhāṣiṇāṃ śiśūnām ālāpaiś ca | sukhavan manyata ity uttareṇānvayaḥ ||8|| kūṭāḥ vitta-śāṭhyādi-bahulā dharmā yeṣu duḥkha-pradhāneṣu ||9||
entries.literal_english: He explains the corrupt motive: a person whose self and senses are captivated by secret arrangements for sexual enjoyment and the like with unchaste, promiscuous women, and by the chatter of sweet-speaking children, thinks himself happy; this construction connects with what follows. Those practices are deceptive, abound in financial trickery and the like, and are dominated by suffering.

entries.sanskrit: भ्रियमाणः पुष्यमाणः ॥१४॥ अवमत्यावज्ञयोपन्यस्तं समीपे प्रक्षिप्तम् । गृह-पालः श्वा । आहरन् भुञ्जानः । आमयावी रोगी ॥१५॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: bhriyamāṇaḥ puṣyamāṇaḥ ||14|| avamatyāvajñayopanyastaṃ samīpe prakṣiptam | gṛha-pālaḥ śvā | āharan bhuñjānaḥ | āmayāvī rogī ||15||
entries.literal_english: Bhriyamāṇaḥ is explained as puṣyamāṇaḥ: being maintained and nourished. Avamatya means “with contempt”; upanyastam is something placed nearby, that is, thrown down. Gṛha-pālaḥ, “house-guardian,” means a dog. Āharan means bhuñjānaḥ, “eating”; āmayāvī means rogī, “sick.”

entries.sanskrit: तयोस् तर्जनैर् निर्भिन्नं हृदयं यस्य । आर्तः संश् चलतीति द्वितीयेनान्वयः ॥२१॥ क्षुत्-तृड्भ्यां परीतो व्याप्तः । तप्ता वालुका यस्मिन् । निर्गत आश्रमो विश्राम-स्थानम् उदकं च यस्मिन् ॥२२॥

transliteration: tayos tarjanair nirbhinnaṃ hṛdayaṃ yasya | ārtaḥ saṃś calatīti dvitīyenānvayaḥ ||21|| kṣut-tṛḍbhyāṃ parīto vyāptaḥ | taptā vālukā yasmin | nirgata āśramo viśrāma-sthānam udakaṃ ca yasmin ||22||
entries.literal_english: His heart is pierced by the threats of those two [messengers]. Being distressed, he moves on; this is connected with the second statement. He is overwhelmed by hunger and thirst. The road has burning sand and lacks both a resting place and water.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रैव विशेषम् आह---अध्वनः सम्बन्धिनां योजनानां नवतिं नव च सहस्राणि पापाधिक्ये द्वाभ्यां वा नीतः सन् ॥२४॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tatraiva viśeṣam āha---adhvanaḥ sambandhināṃ yojanānāṃ navatiṃ nava ca sahasrāṇi pāpādhikye dvābhyāṃ vā nītaḥ san ||24||
entries.literal_english: He specifies the distance: ninety-nine thousand yojanas of road. When the sin is greater, the person is brought in two [muhūrtas]. Here dvābhyām is an alternative duration—two muhūrtas—not “by two” messengers.

entries.sanskrit: ननु पापम् अपि विहाय गच्छतु तत्राह---दैवेनेति । तस्य कुटुम्ब-पोषणस्य शमलं पापं दैवनेनेश्वरेण प्रापितं भुङ्क्ते ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by fate—that is, by the Lord
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu pāpam api vihāya gacchatu tatrāha---daiveneti | tasya kuṭumba-poṣaṇasya śamalaṃ pāpaṃ daivaneneśvareṇa prāpitaṃ bhuṅkte ||32||
entries.literal_english: One might object: “Then let him go, leaving even the sin behind.” The passage answers with “by fate”: he undergoes the stain—the sin—of maintaining his family, which has been brought upon him by the Lord.
